reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

votes.question: On Passage — Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule issued by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to the “California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Commercial Harbor Craft Regulations; Notice of Decision” (H J RES 213)
votes.plain_language: This resolution would cancel the Environmental Protection Agency decision that partly let California tighten emissions rules for commercial harbor boats, including fishing boats. A Yea votes to cancel that decision. A Nay votes to leave it in place.

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–314 of 2026 (314 votes, January 6, 2026 to September 16, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Passage — Sunshine Protection Act (H R 139)
votes.bill_title: Sunshine Protection Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill makes daylight saving time the new, permanent standard time. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Lulu’s Law (S 1003)
votes.bill_title: Lulu’s Law
votes.plain_language: This bill requires the Federal Communications Commission to issue an order explicitly permitting the transmission of wireless emergency alerts to mobile phones in the event of a shark attack. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act (H R 9500)
votes.bill_title: Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act
votes.plain_language: This bill widens the tax deduction for theft and fraud losses, including losses that are not from a declared disaster, and it eases related refund and retirement-plan rules. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Expressing support for tax policies that support working families (H RES 1156)
votes.bill_title: Expressing support for tax policies that support working families.
votes.plain_language: This resolution expresses support for tax policies that support working families and recognizes the tax relief enacted as part of the 2025 reconciliation act. A Yea agrees to the resolution; a Nay opposes it.

topics.topic: Civil Rights and Liberties, Minority Issues

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Agree — Calling on elected officials and civil society leaders to counter antisemitism and educate the public on the contributions of the Jewish-American community (H RES 1251)
votes.bill_title: Calling on elected officials and civil society leaders to counter antisemitism and educate the public on the contributions of the Jewish-American community.
votes.plain_language: This resolution calls on elected officials, faith leaders, and civil society leaders to condemn and counter acts of anti-Semitism. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports agreeing to it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — TRUE Accountability Act (H R 8466)
votes.bill_title: TRUE Accountability Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires agencies to develop and implement plans for preventing fraud and improper payments relating to federal emergency spending (e.g., providing funding relating to disasters or pandemics). This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Haiti Economic Lift Program Extension Act (H R 6504)
votes.bill_title: Haiti Economic Lift Program Extension Act
votes.plain_language: This bill extends through December 31, 2028, the special duty-free rules for various apparel products imported from Haiti. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — EARLY Act Reauthorization (H R 4541)
votes.bill_title: To reauthorize the Young Women’s Breast Health Education and Awareness Requires Learning Young Act of 2009.
votes.plain_language: This bill reauthorizes and revises programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention that support services and education addressing breast and cervical cancer. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Adjourn (ADJOURN)
votes.plain_language: This was a motion to adjourn the House. A Yea votes to adjourn; a Nay votes to stay in session.

votes.question: On Passage — Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884)
votes.bill_title: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act
votes.plain_language: This bill restarts Social Security disability demonstration projects through 2031 and says a participant's total income cannot be reduced. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — ROTOR Act (S 2503)
votes.bill_title: ROTOR Act
votes.plain_language: This bill addresses aviation safety by increasing requirements for aircraft tracking and communication using Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) technology and expanding oversight. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

party_line.scope: House roll calls 1–314 of 2026 (314 votes, January 6, 2026 to September 16, 2026), from the House Clerk.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
